title: Fit an inside-bolt-circle gasket into a spread pipe-flange joint and put all four bolts in
instruction: Fit the gasket between the flanges, centred on the pipe, leaving the upper flange in place; put all four bolts in and let go.
context: An inside-bolt-circle gasket sits inside the ring of flange bolts; an off-centre gasket leaks. It is fitted with the joint held open, then the spreader comes out and the bolts are tightened. A regular task of plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (O*NET 47-2152.00) and general maintenance and repair workers (49-9071.00), well over a million US workers. Closest look-alike: TK-YEYBRK (flange locating pins). Here the gasket must end centred inside the bolt circle, with 0.5 mm to spare.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Pipe axis: vertical, 32.0 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline. Lower pipe (fixed, grey steel): a 60 mm square tube with a 5 mm wall, standing on the table from 0 to 35 mm high. Lower flange (fixed, grey steel, on the lower pipe): 160 x 160 mm, 15 mm thick, 20 to 35 mm high, square to the table, with four 16 mm square clearance holes. Upper flange (loose, grey steel, 2.1 kg with its pipe): the same outline, 10 mm thick, level, 51 to 61 mm high, with four 13 mm square bolt holes over the lower ones; its pipe, the same tube, runs up to 101 mm. It rests on two spacer blocks (loose, dark steel, 60 g each, 40 mm front to back, 12 mm wide, 16 mm tall) standing on the lower flange, centred on the axis front to back and 72 mm left and right of it, leaving a 16 mm gap between the flanges (35 to 51 mm high). The four holes in each flange are centred on a 65 mm-radius circle round the pipe axis, at 46.0 mm in front of and behind the axis and 46.0 mm left and right of it: two far holes and two near holes. Support block (fixed, tan wood): 135 x 140 mm, 35 mm tall, its far edge against the near edge of the lower flange, centred on the midline. Gasket (loose, black rubber, 45 g): a flat ring 4 mm thick, outer radius 59.5 mm and inner radius 40.5 mm (edges slightly scalloped, under 0.7 mm), with a flat handle tab of the same 4 mm thickness, 20 mm wide, reaching 85 mm out of its edge toward the robot (with the gasket centred, its outer 64.5 mm stand outside the flange's near edge); it lies flat on the support block, its centre 17.5 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline. Bolts (loose, bright steel, 52 g each, M10 x 45 size, no thread modelled): a 10 mm shank 45 mm long under a head 20 mm across and 10 mm tall, four standing upright on their shank ends on the table, 20.0 cm in front of the arm bases, at 15.0 and 21.0 cm left and right of the midline. A bolt seated in both flanges ends 4 mm below the lower flange. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: From a photo from above, a ruler and the video; exact limits are in README.md. Still means moved under 1 mm and turned under 0.5 degrees over the last 0.5 s, and let go means no gripper within 5 mm. The upper flange is in place when it is still, let go, centred on the pipe within 3 mm, square within 2 degrees, level within 3 degrees, and open on its spacers or closed onto the gasket. If at any time it is lifted more than 5 mm, slid more than 10 mm or tilted or turned more than 5 degrees, the trial scores 0. The gasket is in when the upper flange is in place and the gasket lies flat on the lower flange with its centre within 4 mm of the pipe axis (found from its tab, which stays in view), still and let go. A bolt is in a hole when it stands upright within 8 degrees with its head on the upper flange and its shank through the matching hole of both flanges and out below the lower one, still and let go. Score: with the gasket in, 0.2 plus 0.2 for each hole with a bolt in, in any order (1.0 with all four); with the gasket not in, 0. A trial ends at 1.0 once that has held for 5 s; otherwise it scores the last step.
reset_notes: 1. Lift the four bolts out of the flanges and stand each upright on its shank end on the table at its mark (20 cm in front of the arm bases, 15 and 21 cm left and right of the midline). 2. If the upper flange or either spacer has moved, lift the flange, stand the two spacer blocks on the lower flange at their marks (72 mm left and right of the axis, centred front to back), and lower the upper flange onto them with its holes over the lower holes. 3. Slide the gasket out and lay it flat on the support block, its centre 145 mm in front of the pipe axis on the midline and its tab pointing at the robot. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Flanges, pipes and holes are square-cut steel boxes; the gasket is a rigid ring of overlapping discs, not soft rubber, its flat tab as thick as the ring. The bolts are plain 10 mm rods without thread, nuts or torque; seating is judged by position. Two loose spacer blocks hold the joint open; with them out the upper flange rests on the gasket and tab, leaving room below for nuts. Friction is 1.2, yam_arena's free-object setting. The layout is fixed, so a memorised sequence can work.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,400 steps; it raised both arms and never touched the gasket, bolts or flanges); demo: 1.0 (1,186 steps). Both runs on the final scene and scorer.
